conflict_group: spawn-destination-foreign-cross-repo-epic-predispatch-bound
Spec-path: packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts
Target-digest: sha256:49d06211c2b5b454057acb3bbde36707ffa7176a468f795132a8a11c00ba8126
dispatch-sha: 60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de
dest: .deft-scratch/worktrees/arc-7270

## In plain English
A parent sitting in one product repo cannot spawn a worker into a linked worktree of the other repo in the same epic, even after swarm:pre-dispatch bound that worktree. The spawn occupancy gate treats any different main worktree root as foreign and refuses. Closed #6871 fixed commit/Write for other repos; this gate is separate. The expected fix is a narrow admit when the foreign linked worktree already has a live pre-dispatch story binding, so the parent can still own the leaf through spawn instead of implementing it.

## Bound remedy
- Keep destination-foreign as the default refuse when mainWorktreeRoot(dest) differs from mainWorktreeRoot(payloadRoot).
- Admit that foreign linked worktree only when swarm:pre-dispatch has a live story-binding record for the dest path under the dest repo common dir.
- On that admit, place child occupancy and dispatch reservation under the dest repo store, not the parent repo store.
- Keep implement-class rules: linked worktree required, primary-path refuse, process-only critic skip unchanged.
- Name the admit in deny recovery text when a foreign dest exists but the binding is missing.
- Add fixtures for bound-admit, missing-binding-refuse, and same-repo path unchanged.
- Reject dropping destination-foreign entirely.
- Reject requiring the parent to re-root its session into the foreign repo before spawn.
- Reject opening #1090 symphony or a new cross-repo epic CLI as this ticket's remedy.
- Reject treating shell access to the foreign worktree as discharge of Gap C leaf ownership.

Reject list: drop-foreign-deny; parent-reroot-required; symphony-1090; shell-as-leaf.

## Injection / swarm lens
This lean changes spawn destination authority, cross-repo worktree identity, and shared occupancy/reservation state. A false admit launches a mutating leaf into another repository. A Prefer-A that keys admit on a record parent-rooted pre-dispatch cannot write, or that persists reservations where later consult cannot see them, fails closed for the dogfood path or breaks unique-reservation.

blocks-the-design: unreachable dest story-binding admit key
Evidence: Prefer-A limb 2 admits only when swarm:pre-dispatch has a live story-binding under the dest repo common dir. Pin `linkedTarget` in packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts requires sameRepoPath(projectCommon, destCommon) and otherwise returns "target … is not a worktree of this repository". `ensureBeginStoryBinding` uses that resolver and never fails begin on a write miss ("never changes begin's exit code; a failed resolution writes nothing"). Parent-rooted begin still records a live delivery-attempt unit for a foreign targetId under the parent project. Pin destination-foreign in spawn-occupancy.ts:638-650 remains an unconditional mainWorktreeRoot mismatch refuse with no binding probe. Issue body dogfood is a parent session in one repo spawning into the other after pre-dispatch "bound" the worktrees.
Failure mode: Bound ships an admit keyed on a dest-common-dir record that lawful parent-rooted pre-dispatch cannot write for the reported foreign dest; begin can look successful while storyBinding is "no record written"; spawn stays destination-foreign; P1–P3 stay unrelieved.
Disposition: remint Bound so the admit key is reachable on that path — widen story-binding target resolution/write (and matching ended-attempt cleanup) to place the record under the foreign dest git-common-dir, or replace the admit key with a closed predicate parent-rooted begin already produces and still keep dest commit-fence coherence. Do not bind limb 2 as written.

sharpens-framing: dest-store consult and leftover release
Evidence: Prefer-A limb 3 says place child occupancy and dispatch reservation under the dest repo store. Pin `existingDispatchReservation` / `releaseLeftoverSpawnReservation` / `persistSpawnReservation` today take storeRoot from the parent payloadRoot; conflict lookup only walks that storeRoot and its mainWorktreeRoot. Foreign dest main is outside that walk.
Failure mode: write-only dest-store placement with parent-store consult misses a just-persisted foreign reservation and can double-mint before dest occupancy.json is live, or leave leftover release looking at the wrong store.
Disposition: on the foreign-admit path, name the same dest repo store for consult conflict lookup, persist, and leftover release — not persist alone.

footnote: destination-foreign deny text matches pin
Pin consultDeny message for destination-foreign matches the issue Deny block ("linked worktree of a foreign repository" / "linked worktree of this repo"). Limb 1 keep-default-refuse and limb 5 missing-binding recovery text are the right thin shape once the admit key is reachable.

footnote: thin Prefer-A shape otherwise holds
Keep default destination-foreign, linked-worktree / primary-path / process-only critic rules, fixtures, and the Reject list (drop-foreign-deny; parent-reroot-required; symphony-1090; shell-as-leaf). Do not thicken with #1090 or parent re-root.

road-not-taken: parent delivery-attempt unit as sole admit key
Steelmanning Prefer-A: dest-common-dir story-binding is the SoT dest commit/Write already reads for story selection (#6379), so spawn-only use of the parent `.deft/delivery-attempts` unit would open Gap C while leaving the dest fence unbound. Flip condition: keep Prefer-A’s dest-binding admit only if Bound also widens the foreign write/cleanup path so parent-rooted begin actually deposits that record.

Round 1, open critique. Input ceiling: 7133379868. Reviewed Prefer-A draft 7133373863, issue body, Stop 1, spend amendment, and panel deposit within that ceiling. Source verification used git show at 60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de; no product implementation or fixture execution. This is a source-derived design verdict, not a runtime reproduction of the reported incident.

## C1 — blocks-the-design: define what makes a story binding live

Evidence: at the dispatch SHA, packages/core/src/swarm/story-binding-record.ts defines StoryBindingRecord as story_id, worktree_path, and attempt_ids. readStoryBindingRecord validates shape and canonical destination but does not establish attempt liveness; parseRecord accepts an empty attempt_ids array. ensureStoryBindingRecord retains attempt IDs unknown to the caller's ledgers. In packages/core/src/swarm/pre-dispatch.ts, complete/cancel saves the ledger before removing binding IDs, and removal can fail on the store lock. The record-store comments explicitly describe cooperative story selection, not an authorization credential.

Concrete failure: a completed attempt can leave a valid-looking record behind. Treating successful read/nonempty IDs as the draft's "live story-binding" would admit a foreign spawn without a current pre-dispatch attempt. Conversely, checking only a convenient destination checkout's ledger can reject a valid attempt recorded by another checkout. The record itself does not identify its ledger owner. This matters because the proposal promotes story-selection state into an exception to a repository boundary.

Disposition: the lean cannot bind with "live" left as an assumed property of that reader. Specify the authoritative liveness witness and how it is resolved for this destination; missing, malformed, empty, ended, or unverifiable evidence must not grant the exception. Reuse the existing binding and delivery-attempt mechanisms where sufficient; do not introduce a cross-repo orchestration platform. If the intended contract is merely valid binding presence within the existing same-user cooperative trust model, state and justify that weaker predicate explicitly instead of claiming liveness. Add a stale-record-after-failed-cleanup fixture and a valid-binding-from-another-checkout fixture alongside the happy path.

## C2 — sharpens-framing: destination-store ownership is a lifecycle invariant

Evidence: pinned spawn-occupancy.ts consults existingDispatchReservation(payloadRoot, destPath), releases leftovers using payloadRoot, and builds a parent-owned dispatch record. hooks/dispatcher.ts calls persistSpawnReservation(payloadRoot, reservation). Persistence already uses an exclusive destination lock and checks live occupancy again after consult. allocatedWorktreeMatches additionally requires store and candidate to belong to the same repository and checks the presented incarnation and parent. destIsProven also requires matching common directories and influences the parent ritual path.

Concrete failure: moving only the write to the destination store leaves lookup or leftover cleanup aimed at the parent store, so an unlaunched dispatch can remain reserved and block retry. A reader still rooted at the parent can also fail to recognize an allocated foreign destination. With parents from two repositories targeting one destination, separate store selection would defeat the intended single reservation namespace.

Disposition: the draft's destination-store choice is sound and can bind, but state it as consistent consult/persist/retry/release ownership while retaining parent identity and incarnation checks. Preserve existing exclusive-lock and live-occupant controls. Add lifecycle fixtures: two different-repository parents contend for one destination and only one reserves; failed launch can release and retry; stale-incarnation cleanup cannot release a successor; the child starts with the destination root and can claim its reservation. Explicitly decide the foreign destination's destProven/ritual behavior rather than changing it accidentally through a same-repo predicate. These are implementation obligations of the proposed store move, not a new subsystem.

## Existing mechanisms and alternative considered

The pinned destination-foreign branch confirms the reported unconditional cross-repository denial. Existing binding resolution, delivery-attempt state, canonical worktree identity, exclusive destination locks, child occupancy, and incarnation-scoped cleanup provide the relevant mechanisms. pre-dispatch's linkedTarget requires the invocation project and target to share a common directory, and binding failure does not change begin's exit code. Recovery therefore needs a destination-repository invocation and verification of its story-binding result; a generic "run pre-dispatch" from the parent repository is insufficient. This does not require relocating the parent session.

Keeping the unconditional foreign deny has the strongest simple isolation argument, but leaves the stated two-repository leaf workflow blocked. I favor a narrow exception once C1 is resolved and the C2 lifecycle is verified. Dropping the deny entirely is unnecessary. Neither an epic-membership registry nor #1090 is required by these findings. A same-user-writable binding is not protection against a hostile same-user process; do not imply that this patch creates that security boundary.

Critic exit: return to the parent for this round's synthesis; no ingest or implementation.

Pain-audit of Prefer-A Bound 7133821599. Input ceiling: 7133821599. Reviewed the issue body and comments through that ceiling, including Round-1 critics 7133690048 and 7133794843. Verification used git show at 60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de for the design-critique contract, story-binding-record.ts, pre-dispatch.ts, and spawn-occupancy.ts. Source-derived design verdict; no fixture execution or incident reproduction.

## PA1 — blocks-the-design: originating-ledger resolution remains unspecified

Bound improves C1 by requiring an actually open attempt rather than treating record presence as liveness. However, "the delivery-attempt ledger of the project that began it" names the desired witness without specifying how spawn resolves that witness. This is the unresolved half of Codex C1, not a new subsystem request.

Evidence: pinned StoryBindingRecord contains only story_id, worktree_path, and attempt_ids. parseRecord preserves only those fields. pre-dispatch saves ledgers under input.projectRoot; endedAttemptIds explicitly treats another checkout's unknown attempt as unknown, not ended. ensureStoryBindingRecord retains such IDs. Widening the destination binding write does not supply originating-checkout provenance. The Bound adds neither a resolvable owner reference nor a restriction tying the admissible witness to a specified invoking checkout. Repository identity alone does not select a checkout-local ledger.

Concrete failure: checkout A begins a valid attempt and deposits the binding in destination B's common directory. A spawn from another checkout of A, or another permitted parent, can read that binding but cannot determine where its attempt is recorded. Checking the convenient parent or destination ledger falsely refuses a valid binding; treating an unknown ID as still open admits stale evidence. The Bound's empty/all-ended cases do not settle unknown-owner evidence. Its same-store cleanup promise also needs a way for completion to resolve the foreign store after begin.

Disposition: do not bind the current harvest as fully disposing C1. Add one thin mechanism clause defining the authoritative ledger locator (or an explicit supported invocation restriction), validating that the open attempt belongs to this story and canonical destination, and denying unverifiable evidence. Reuse binding and delivery-attempt state; no epic registry or #1090. Cover a valid attempt begun from another checkout, unreadable/unknown owner evidence, and stale binding after failed cleanup. Exact storage syntax can remain an implementation choice; the ownership/resolution contract cannot. This changes the harvested mechanism, hence harvest-changed: true.

## footnote: the other Round-1 dispositions are substantially addressed

Widen-foreign-binding-write directly addresses Grok's unreachable destination-binding writer and includes matching end/cancel cleanup. Dest-store-lifecycle addresses both critics' central consult/persist/release split and retains parent identity and incarnation checks; the contention fixture is appropriate. metadata.issueBody:
## What happened

Phase 6 of deftai/evolution#1840 is one epic in two repositories, deftai/evolution and deftai/deftvisage. The runbook sends one worker per story into a worktree of the repo that owns the code. From a Grok session rooted in evolution I created deftvisage worktrees, wrote the briefs, ran preflight, and `swarm:pre-dispatch` bound them. `spawn_subagent` with `cwd` set to those worktrees was refused.

## Deny

```
Directive denied spawn: destination /Users/johnmcdaniel/Projects/WarpDev/DEFTvisage/.deft-scratch/worktrees/desk-health-flows is a linked worktree of a foreign repository. Spawned mutating work takes a linked worktree of this repo.
```

The same deny fired for `desk-job-snapshot-cards` and `desk-plan-create-guard`.

## Where

`vendor/directive-core/dist/session/spawn-occupancy.js` returns `destination-foreign` when `mainWorktreeRoot(dest)` and `mainWorktreeRoot(payloadRoot)` differ.

## Expected

A parent whose epic already spans two product repos can spawn a leaf into a linked worktree of the other repo after `swarm:pre-dispatch` has bound that worktree to its story. Shell access to that worktree is not a substitute. The parent is not allowed to implement the leaf itself.

## Not the same as

Closed #6871 covered commit and Write hooks refusing other repos. This is the spawn occupancy gate. #1090 is a future cross-operator tier, not this deny.
